A name is a disclosure too

Secret scanners look for values. In a public repo the NAME of a vault, an item or a home directory already tells a reader where to aim. This change scrubs both shapes and adds a test that fails when either comes back.

2vault or item names in tracked files
47home path occurrences, 15 files
0secret values involved
1new security test, static, fails on a reintroduced path

Why a value scanner cannot see it

gitleaks and the content secret scanner match token shapes and entropy. A path like op://Vault/Item/credential has neither. Only a human reviewer caught the last two instances (#2814, #4167).

commit with a real op:// path→ gitleaks: no token shape, pass→ content scanner: no key pattern, pass→ public repo now names the vault and the item
What it meansThe gate that should have caught it was never looking for this.
If we do nothingThe next generated config or Lab page ships the next name.

What changed, before and after

before

const HQ_API_TOKEN_REFERENCE = "op://Vault/Item/credential";
docs: rotate op://Vault/Item/credential
tests: /Users/<real-name>/coding/... in three fixtures

after

const HQ_API_TOKEN_REFERENCE =
  process.env.HQ_API_TOKEN_REFERENCE || "op://<vault>/<item>/credential";
docs: rotate op://<vault>/<item>/credential
tests: /Users/me/coding/...

The announce script still names the real rotation target at runtime: the workflow passes a repository variable, and an empty variable falls back to the placeholder. Nothing deployment-specific is committed.

What it meansSame behaviour in CI, generic text in the repo.
If we do nothingEvery 401 message keeps pointing at a named vault in a public log.

The new gate, and what it accepts

tests/security/test-public-surface-names.sh greps tracked files for two shapes and fails on any hit that is not a placeholder. Try a line below; the same rules run in the test.

type something

Placeholders that pass: a vault or item that starts with <, $, {, or reads as vault, your, my, example; a home directory named me, foo, john, test, dev, someone, alice, bob and the other documentation stand-ins listed in the test.

What it meansA real name fails pre-push and CI; a stand-in passes.
If we do nothingReview stays the only control, and review missed it twice.
